newsitem.title: UK: LME sees changes from Euro currency introduction.
newsitem.headline: LME sees changes from Euro currency introduction.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) said its contracts quoted in sterling or German marks could be affected by the introduction of a new Euro currency, currently envisaged for January 1 1999, the LME said in a notice.

Although still some time away, the Euro is of immediate relevance to LME contracts which are due to mature after January 1 1999, at least where they include payment obligations in a European currency replaced by the Euro.

LME contracts likely to be affected are those governed by English law, where payment obligations fall due in sterling or German marks after January 1 1999, assuming these to be participating currencies.
Two regulations proposed by the European Commission relating to the introduction of the Euro are likely to have some bearing on these contracts.
Under the first, relating to the transitional phase, LME parties may perform their obligations in sterling or in German marks, as the case may be, or, if the paying party so chooses, the Euro.
Under the second, the parties must perform the obligations in Euros (calculated at the relevant conversion rate).

If either sterling of German marks are not participating national currencies, then the introduction of the Euro should not affect the terms of any LME contract where the payment obligations fall due in such currency, the LME said.

It added that the proposed council regulations will not affect non-LME contracts which are governed by the law of jurisdictions not participating in the European Monetary Union, for example New York law contracts.
